item.title: Youngstown Library celebrates start of Lunar New Year
item.description: The Lunar New Year kicked off Tuesday, marking the start of the new year according to the lunar calendar.

item.title: Death penalty still being decided in postal worker murder in Warren
item.description: Federal prosecutors are still deciding on a death penalty specification in the murder case of a Warren postal worker, with a jury trial set for August 17th.

item.title: West 34 reopens after downtown heating problems
item.description: The eatery was forced to shut down three weeks ago because of heating problems with SOBE Thermal Energy -- which then led to water line breaks in the building.

item.title: Trumbull County EMA preparing to move to new location
item.description: Standing outside the old Bazetta Fire Station, Director John Hickey spoke about the benefits of moving the EMA near the county fairgrounds.

item.title: Diocese sees largest group since 2014 to join Roman Catholic Church
item.description: About 282 men, women and children from the Diocese of Youngstown will attend the Rite of Election service led by Bishop David Bonnar, marking a significant increase in people joining the Catholic Church.

item.title: Animal Charity rescues 58 animals in one day, asks community for help
item.description: Animal Charity of Ohio removed 58 animals from dangerous situations in a single day Tuesday, according to a press release.

item.title: Local pastor remembers civil rights leader Jesse Jackson as friend
item.description: Many people saw Rev. Jesse Jackson as a political figure, but he was more of a friend to a local pastor.

item.title: Area reopens after crash involving police cruiser, three taken to hospital
item.description: Three people were taken to the hospital after a crash involving a police cruiser Tuesday evening in Boardman.

item.title: Poland Twp. police chief testifies before committee to allow for resource officer at Holy Family
item.description: Poland Township Police Chief Greg Wilson testified Tuesday before the Senate Education Committee in Columbus, urging them to change the law to allow the township to continue providing a student resource police officer to Holy Family Catholic School.

item.title: Elections Board will not move to downtown building
item.description: The Mahoning County Board of Elections unanimously passed a resolution Tuesday evening stating they will not move into a new Mahoning County administration building being proposed for downtown Youngstown.
